title: policy-compiler-residency-audit-sampler-kms-path-sanitizer
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a declarative residency policy compiler that emits OPA bundles, an audit-sampling shim for high-volume non-critical calls, and a KMS resource path sanitizer to canonicalize provider bindings. No user-facing API changes; rollout behind feature flag. Backfills audit retention TTL for sampled records.
description:
Context: customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need a deterministic way to express data residency constraints and get reproducible enforcement + succinct audit trails. This PR delivers three coordinated pieces: (1) a policy compiler that converts high-level residency rules (service-level claims, geozone allows/denies, operator exceptions) into compact OPA bundles suitable for runtime evaluation and policy diffing; (2) an audit-sampling shim that reduces storage and ingest costs by sampling non-residency-impacting requests while preserving dense traces for cross-region or KMS-bound events; (3) a KMS path sanitizer that normalizes provider-specific KMS resource paths into a canonical internal form so residency checks and audit indexing are reliable regardless of KMS provider syntax. Motivation: previous enforcement relied on distributed ad-hoc checks that led to mismatches between audit logs and RBAC decision outcomes, and caused several edge-case incidents where a KMS ARN variant bypassed residency matching. This implementation centralizes the translation and makes decision artifacts auditable and diffable.

What I changed (summary):
- pkg/policy/compiler: new IR -> OPA translator that accepts residency rule YAML and emits a policy bundle (policy metadata, constraints, fingerprint). The compiler includes a small optimizer to dedupe overlapping allow rules.
- pkg/audit/sampler: introduces a sampling policy engine (configurable sampling rates by route, by geozone, with overrides for KMS-bound ops) and a retention metadata marker for sampled records so the audit-store can apply TTLs.
- pkg/kms/sanitizer: canonicalizes provider variants (AWS ARN, GCP resource-name, Azure keyvault URIs) into a stable key identifier used by policy and audit subsystems.
- cmd/policyctl: CLI additions to lint, compile, and preview residency bundles; added `policyctl diff --live` to compare compiled bundle against runtime decisions for canary/rollouts.
- helm/redwood/templates/rbacv2.yaml: feature-flag gates and RBAC templates to enable the compiler and sampling shim in staged rollout.
- docs/security/residency-compiler.md: specification and examples for writing residency rules, sampling profiles, and KMS canonicalization rules.
- tests/*: unit and e2e tests covering translation correctness, sampler determinism (seeded), and sanitizer idempotence.

Checklist: - [x] Compiler emits OPA bundle and fingerprint metadata - [x] Sampler marks records and exposes retention hint header - [x] Sanitizer covers AWS/GCP/Azure syntaxes and includes unknown-provider fallback - [x] End-to-end test against policy mock service - [x] Telemetry counters (policy.compile.success/fail, audit.sampler.sampled, kms.sanitize.mapped)

Security notes: sampler retains high-fidelity traces when a residency decision is NOT a simple allow (i.e., any deny, cross-region, or uncertain decisions are always fully retained). Sanitizer rejects unknown providers by returning a decision 'unknown_kms_format' which surfaces in the audit stream and increments a security alert metric to prompt operator review.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind `residency_compiler` and `audit_sampler` toggles. Default off for existing clusters. Gradual rollout to staged tenants with canary bundles via `policyctl diff` and a 48h monitoring window. If mismatch rate > 0.5% for canary tenants (measured as diffed decisions vs current runtime), rollback the feature flag and open ENG-rollback Linear task.

Related work: builds on ENG-2145's residency schema and extends the earlier kms-normalizer prototype from SEC-402. See linked Linear tasks for design notes and attack surface review.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can the compiler attach stable fingerprints when rule reordering occurs? I want diffs to be meaningful across minor reorderings.
Asha Kapoor: Yes — the compiler normalizes rule ordering and computes a semantic fingerprint (sha256 of normalized AST). Added tests for reorder invariance.
Maya Li: Audit sampling policy seems risky for high-security tenants. We should ensure opt-out and per-tenant whitelist.
Asha Kapoor: sampling is opt-in per tenant by default; for enterprise tenants the default sampling rate is 0 and there is a per-tenant policy override. Added config and docs.
Evan Brooks: KMS sanitizer mapping should fail closed on unknown formats. Prefer returning explicit decision and incrementing alert counter.
Asha Kapoor: Agreed, implemented unknown_kms_format decision and metric kms.sanitize.unknown (see tests).
Diego Alvarez: CI flake on e2e was due to race in sampler metrics — re-run fixed it. Approving post-fix.
Maya Li: Security review complete, no blockers. Approving.
